root_cause.text: The hugetlb early-boot command-line parser (`hugetlb_add_param()` in `mm/hugetlb.c`) assumed its input string was non-NULL, so when `hugepages`, `hugepagesz`, or `default_hugepagesz` were given without an `=` separator the early parameter code passed NULL and the function later dereferenced it in `strlen()`, causing a boot-time crash.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit message states that “early parameter parsing passes NULL to hugetlb_add_param(), which dereferences it in strlen() and can crash the system,” and the patch fixes this by adding `if (!s) return -EINVAL;` at the start of `hugetlb_add_param()` before any `strlen()`-related processing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a null check in hugetlb parameter parsing to reject missing input with -EINVAL.
intent_record.what: A null-pointer check was added at the start of `hugetlb_add_param(char *s, int (*setup)(char *))`; if `s` is `NULL`, the function now immediately returns `-EINVAL` before any further processing.
intent_record.how: This prevents the function from dereferencing or otherwise operating on a null command-line parameter string, causing the call to fail cleanly with an invalid-argument error instead of risking a crash or undefined behavior.

grouping_result.intent: Add a null check in hugetlb parameter parsing to reject missing input with -EINVAL.

In this snippet, the parser is `hugepages_setup(char *s)`, which begins by operating on `char *p = s` and then parses only `hugepages=` values. There is no dereference of an assumed-non-NULL separator-dependent pointer here, and the old unsafe `sscanf(s, "%lu", mhp)` / implicit assumption about input structure is gone.
